title: Indian-American Oncologist Wins OSU Innovator Award
excerpt: Dr. Akshay Sood's cancer-detection breakthroughs earn Ohio State's 2026 Early Career Innovator of the Year honor
body:
Dr. Akshay Sood, an Indian-American urologic oncologist at The Ohio State University, claimed the 2026 Early Career Innovator of the Year Award on April 7 — recognition that signals a new chapter in cancer diagnostics.

**What the award recognizes:**
Ohio State's Enterprise for Research, Innovation and Knowledge (ERIK) grants this award to researchers who advance university intellectual property, patents, and licensed technology — and Sood earned it for his creativity, collaborative spirit, and entrepreneurial drive that makes a tangible impact on patient care. Sood himself credits the patients he sees as the inspiration behind all of his work.

**The science behind the honor:**
Sood has created a first-in-class, flexible biopsy instrument designed to obtain full-thickness tissue samples from luminal organs — currently undergoing patent application — with the potential to transform cancer diagnostics, enabling more accurate staging and personalized treatment. His research has also produced provisional patents for an allograft bioengineered conduit device for urinary diversion, a micro-nanofluidic device enabling rapid, non-invasive detection of tumor DNA in urinary extracellular vesicles, and an ink-based biopsy orientation sampling innovation to enhance precision mapping in prostate cancer diagnosis.

**A record that speaks for itself:**
Sood has authored more than 225 research papers, editorials, and book chapters in journals including *JAMA Internal Medicine*, *Journal of Clinical Oncology*, *BMJ*, and *European Urology*. He has also received the prestigious John D. Silbar Award from the American Urological Association and the Michael S. Benninger Award from Wayne State University School of Medicine.

**What to watch:**
Sood's biopsy instrument and micro-nanofluidic DNA-detection device are moving through the patent process — watch for commercialization milestones and clinical trial results that could reshape how urologic cancers are staged and treated.
